subtype: Approach: talking to Indians already living there [Action]
passage:
Neelam had a shiny brochure from a consultancy and a lot of questions it did not answer. On a Sunday in her Mumbai flat, she wrote a short message and sent it to five professionals she found through an alumni group who lived in Toronto.
"I'm thinking of moving. Could you tell me what rent really costs, what tax takes, how long your job hunt took, and whether it gets lonely?"
By Wednesday four had replied. Rent was higher than the brochure said. One had needed five months to find a job. Abhinav wrote the longest note: the first winter was the hardest, and he had called home every night.
Neelam read them at the kitchen table, unsettled and grateful in equal measure, and made a fresh list of questions.

qa.q: How many professionals did Neelam message?
What was Neelam feeling as she read the replies?
qa.a: Neelam was unsettled and grateful at once, learning things the brochure had left out.

qa.q: What could Neelam do with the fresh list of questions?
qa.a: Neelam could ask the same people, and a few others, and compare their answers before making any decision.

qa.q: How might Abhinav have felt writing the longest note?
qa.a: Abhinav was probably remembering his hard first winter and wanted to be honest so that Neelam would be prepared.

grounding: The passage shows a person messaging five professionals in the target city about rent, taxes, job hunting time and loneliness to get a picture beyond brochures.
